"""A tiny algebra over HALF-OPEN integer intervals [start, end).

Half-open semantics (READ THIS before changing behavior):
  * An interval [start, end) covers x iff ``start <= x < end``.
  * An interval with ``start >= end`` is EMPTY and is ignored.

Canonical form:
  The IntervalSet maintains its internal state as a SORTED list of
  non-overlapping intervals. ``add(start, end)`` inserts the new interval and
  coalesces it with any intervals it strictly OVERLAPS (two intervals overlap
  when they share at least one covered x, i.e. ``max(start_a, start_b)
  < min(end_a, end_b)``). Merely-touching neighbours (one interval's end
  equal to the next one's start) are currently left as separate intervals.

Public API:
  add(start, end), intervals(), raw(), contains(x)
"""


class IntervalSet:
    def __init__(self):
        # Canonical store: sorted by start, pairwise non-overlapping (touching
        # endpoints permitted for now), every interval non-empty.
        self._intervals = []

    def add(self, start, end):
        """Insert [start, end), coalescing it into the canonical form.

        Empty intervals (start >= end) are ignored. Intervals that merely
        touch the new interval (end == next start) are not merged.
        """
        if start >= end:
            return
        lo, hi = start, end
        merged = []
        placed = False
        for a, b in self._intervals:
            if a >= hi:
                # Interval starts at/after the growing span ends: touch or
                # beyond, so it stays separate -- drop the span in first.
                if not placed:
                    merged.append((lo, hi))
                    placed = True
                merged.append((a, b))
            elif b <= lo:
                # Interval ends at/before the span starts: touch or behind.
                merged.append((a, b))
            else:
                # Strictly overlaps the growing span: coalesce it in.
                lo = min(lo, a)
                hi = max(hi, b)
        if not placed:
            merged.append((lo, hi))
        self._intervals = merged

    def intervals(self):
        """Return the sorted, merged list of (start, end) tuples."""
        return list(self._intervals)

    def raw(self):
        """Backwards-compatible alias of intervals(): the merged, sorted form.

        (With a canonical store there is no longer an insertion-order history;
        this name is kept so callers of the seed API keep working.)
        """
        return list(self._intervals)

    def contains(self, x):
        """True iff any interval covers x (start <= x < end)."""
        for s, e in self._intervals:
            if s <= x < e:
                return True
        return False

"""A tiny algebra over HALF-OPEN integer intervals [start, end).

Half-open semantics (READ THIS before changing behavior):
  * An interval [start, end) covers x iff ``start <= x < end``.
  * An interval with ``start >= end`` is EMPTY and is ignored.

Canonical form:
  The IntervalSet maintains its internal state as a SORTED list of
  non-overlapping intervals. ``add(start, end)`` inserts the new interval and
  coalesces it with any intervals it strictly OVERLAPS (two intervals overlap
  when they share at least one covered x, i.e. ``max(start_a, start_b)
  < min(end_a, end_b)``). Merely-touching neighbours (one interval's end
  equal to the next one's start) are currently left as separate intervals.

Public API:
  add(start, end), intervals(), raw(), contains(x)
"""


class IntervalSet:
    def __init__(self):
        # Canonical store: sorted by start, pairwise non-overlapping (touching
        # endpoints permitted for now), every interval non-empty.
        self._intervals = []

    def add(self, start, end):
        """Insert [start, end), coalescing it into the canonical form.

        Empty intervals (start >= end) are ignored. Intervals that merely
        touch the new interval (end == next start) are not merged.
        """
        if start >= end:
            return
        lo, hi = start, end
        merged = []
        placed = False
        for a, b in self._intervals:
            if a >= hi:
                # Interval starts at/after the growing span ends: touch or
                # beyond, so it stays separate -- drop the span in first.
                if not placed:
                    merged.append((lo, hi))
                    placed = True
                merged.append((a, b))
            elif b <= lo:
                # Interval ends at/before the span starts: touch or behind.
                merged.append((a, b))
            else:
                # Strictly overlaps the growing span: coalesce it in.
                lo = min(lo, a)
                hi = max(hi, b)
        if not placed:
            merged.append((lo, hi))
        self._intervals = merged

    def intervals(self):
        """Return the sorted, merged list of (start, end) tuples."""
        return list(self._intervals)

    def raw(self):
        """Backwards-compatible alias of intervals(): the merged, sorted form.

        (With a canonical store there is no longer an insertion-order history;
        this name is kept so callers of the seed API keep working.)
        """
        return list(self._intervals)

    def contains(self, x):
        """True iff any interval covers x (start <= x < end)."""
        for s, e in self._intervals:
            if s <= x < e:
                return True
        return False

"""A tiny algebra over HALF-OPEN integer intervals [start, end).

Half-open semantics (READ THIS before changing behavior):
  * An interval [start, end) covers x iff ``start <= x < end``.
  * An interval with ``start >= end`` is EMPTY and is ignored.

Canonical form:
  The IntervalSet maintains its internal state as a SORTED list of
  non-overlapping intervals. ``add(start, end)`` inserts the new interval and
  coalesces it with any intervals it strictly OVERLAPS (two intervals overlap
  when they share at least one covered x, i.e. ``max(start_a, start_b)
  < min(end_a, end_b)``). Merely-touching neighbours (one interval's end
  equal to the next one's start) are currently left as separate intervals.

Public API:
  add(start, end), intervals(), raw(), contains(x)
"""


class IntervalSet:
    def __init__(self):
        # Canonical store: sorted by start, pairwise non-overlapping (touching
        # endpoints permitted for now), every interval non-empty.
        self._intervals = []

    def add(self, start, end):
        """Insert [start, end), coalescing it into the canonical form.

        Empty intervals (start >= end) are ignored. Intervals that merely
        touch the new interval (end == next start) are not merged.
        """
        if start >= end:
            return
        lo, hi = start, end
        merged = []
        placed = False
        for a, b in self._intervals:
            if a >= hi:
                # Interval starts at/after the growing span ends: touch or
                # beyond, so it stays separate -- drop the span in first.
                if not placed:
                    merged.append((lo, hi))
                    placed = True
                merged.append((a, b))
            elif b <= lo:
                # Interval ends at/before the span starts: touch or behind.
                merged.append((a, b))
            else:
                # Strictly overlaps the growing span: coalesce it in.
                lo = min(lo, a)
                hi = max(hi, b)
        if not placed:
            merged.append((lo, hi))
        self._intervals = merged

    def intervals(self):
        """Return the sorted, merged list of (start, end) tuples."""
        return list(self._intervals)

    def raw(self):
        """Backwards-compatible alias of intervals(): the merged, sorted form.

        (With a canonical store there is no longer an insertion-order history;
        this name is kept so callers of the seed API keep working.)
        """
        return list(self._intervals)

    def contains(self, x):
        """True iff any interval covers x (start <= x < end)."""
        for s, e in self._intervals:
            if s <= x < e:
                return True
        return False

"""A tiny algebra over HALF-OPEN integer intervals [start, end).

Half-open semantics (READ THIS before changing behavior):
  * An interval [start, end) covers x iff ``start <= x < end``.
  * An interval with ``start >= end`` is EMPTY and is ignored.

Canonical form:
  The IntervalSet maintains its internal state as a SORTED list of
  non-overlapping intervals. ``add(start, end)`` inserts the new interval and
  coalesces it with any intervals it strictly OVERLAPS (two intervals overlap
  when they share at least one covered x, i.e. ``max(start_a, start_b)
  < min(end_a, end_b)``). Merely-touching neighbours (one interval's end
  equal to the next one's start) are currently left as separate intervals.

Public API:
  add(start, end), intervals(), raw(), contains(x)
"""


class IntervalSet:
    def __init__(self):
        # Canonical store: sorted by start, pairwise non-overlapping (touching
        # endpoints permitted for now), every interval non-empty.
        self._intervals = []

    def add(self, start, end):
        """Insert [start, end), coalescing it into the canonical form.

        Empty intervals (start >= end) are ignored. Intervals that merely
        touch the new interval (end == next start) are not merged.
        """
        if start >= end:
            return
        lo, hi = start, end
        merged = []
        placed = False
        for a, b in self._intervals:
            if a >= hi:
                # Interval starts at/after the growing span ends: touch or
                # beyond, so it stays separate -- drop the span in first.
                if not placed:
                    merged.append((lo, hi))
                    placed = True
                merged.append((a, b))
            elif b <= lo:
                # Interval ends at/before the span starts: touch or behind.
                merged.append((a, b))
            else:
                # Strictly overlaps the growing span: coalesce it in.
                lo = min(lo, a)
                hi = max(hi, b)
        if not placed:
            merged.append((lo, hi))
        self._intervals = merged

    def intervals(self):
        """Return the sorted, merged list of (start, end) tuples."""
        return list(self._intervals)

    def raw(self):
        """Backwards-compatible alias of intervals(): the merged, sorted form.

        (With a canonical store there is no longer an insertion-order history;
        this name is kept so callers of the seed API keep working.)
        """
        return list(self._intervals)

    def contains(self, x):
        """True iff any interval covers x (start <= x < end)."""
        for s, e in self._intervals:
            if s <= x < e:
                return True
        return False

"""A tiny algebra over HALF-OPEN integer intervals [start, end).

Half-open semantics (READ THIS before changing behavior):
  * An interval [start, end) covers x iff ``start <= x < end``.
  * An interval with ``start >= end`` is EMPTY and is ignored.

Canonical form:
  The IntervalSet maintains its internal state as a SORTED list of
  non-overlapping intervals. ``add(start, end)`` inserts the new interval and
  coalesces it with any intervals it strictly OVERLAPS (two intervals overlap
  when they share at least one covered x, i.e. ``max(start_a, start_b)
  < min(end_a, end_b)``). Merely-touching neighbours (one interval's end
  equal to the next one's start) are currently left as separate intervals.

Public API:
  add(start, end), intervals(), raw(), contains(x)
"""


class IntervalSet:
    def __init__(self):
        # Canonical store: sorted by start, pairwise non-overlapping (touching
        # endpoints permitted for now), every interval non-empty.
        self._intervals = []

    def add(self, start, end):
        """Insert [start, end), coalescing it into the canonical form.

        Empty intervals (start >= end) are ignored. Intervals that merely
        touch the new interval (end == next start) are not merged.
        """
        if start >= end:
            return
        lo, hi = start, end
        merged = []
        placed = False
        for a, b in self._intervals:
            if a >= hi:
                # Interval starts at/after the growing span ends: touch or
                # beyond, so it stays separate -- drop the span in first.
                if not placed:
                    merged.append((lo, hi))
                    placed = True
                merged.append((a, b))
            elif b <= lo:
                # Interval ends at/before the span starts: touch or behind.
                merged.append((a, b))
            else:
                # Strictly overlaps the growing span: coalesce it in.
                lo = min(lo, a)
                hi = max(hi, b)
        if not placed:
            merged.append((lo, hi))
        self._intervals = merged

    def intervals(self):
        """Return the sorted, merged list of (start, end) tuples."""
        return list(self._intervals)

    def raw(self):
        """Backwards-compatible alias of intervals(): the merged, sorted form.

        (With a canonical store there is no longer an insertion-order history;
        this name is kept so callers of the seed API keep working.)
        """
        return list(self._intervals)

    def contains(self, x):
        """True iff any interval covers x (start <= x < end)."""
        for s, e in self._intervals:
            if s <= x < e:
                return True
        return False

"""A tiny algebra over HALF-OPEN integer intervals [start, end).

Half-open semantics (READ THIS before changing behavior):
  * An interval [start, end) covers x iff ``start <= x < end``.
  * An interval with ``start >= end`` is EMPTY and is ignored.

Canonical form:
  The IntervalSet maintains its internal state as a SORTED list of
  non-overlapping intervals. ``add(start, end)`` inserts the new interval and
  coalesces it with any intervals it strictly OVERLAPS (two intervals overlap
  when they share at least one covered x, i.e. ``max(start_a, start_b)
  < min(end_a, end_b)``). Merely-touching neighbours (one interval's end
  equal to the next one's start) are currently left as separate intervals.

Public API:
  add(start, end), intervals(), raw(), contains(x)
"""


class IntervalSet:
    def __init__(self):
        # Canonical store: sorted by start, pairwise non-overlapping (touching
        # endpoints permitted for now), every interval non-empty.
        self._intervals = []

    def add(self, start, end):
        """Insert [start, end), coalescing it into the canonical form.

        Empty intervals (start >= end) are ignored. Intervals that merely
        touch the new interval (end == next start) are not merged.
        """
        if start >= end:
            return
        lo, hi = start, end
        merged = []
        placed = False
        for a, b in self._intervals:
            if a >= hi:
                # Interval starts at/after the growing span ends: touch or
                # beyond, so it stays separate -- drop the span in first.
                if not placed:
                    merged.append((lo, hi))
                    placed = True
                merged.append((a, b))
            elif b <= lo:
                # Interval ends at/before the span starts: touch or behind.
                merged.append((a, b))
            else:
                # Strictly overlaps the growing span: coalesce it in.
                lo = min(lo, a)
                hi = max(hi, b)
        if not placed:
            merged.append((lo, hi))
        self._intervals = merged

    def intervals(self):
        """Return the sorted, merged list of (start, end) tuples."""
        return list(self._intervals)

    def raw(self):
        """Backwards-compatible alias of intervals(): the merged, sorted form.

        (With a canonical store there is no longer an insertion-order history;
        this name is kept so callers of the seed API keep working.)
        """
        return list(self._intervals)

    def contains(self, x):
        """True iff any interval covers x (start <= x < end)."""
        for s, e in self._intervals:
            if s <= x < e:
                return True
        return False

"""A tiny algebra over HALF-OPEN integer intervals [start, end).

Half-open semantics (READ THIS before changing behavior):
  * An interval [start, end) covers x iff ``start <= x < end``.
  * An interval with ``start >= end`` is EMPTY and is ignored.

Canonical form:
  The IntervalSet maintains its internal state as a SORTED list of
  non-overlapping intervals. ``add(start, end)`` inserts the new interval and
  coalesces it with any intervals it strictly OVERLAPS (two intervals overlap
  when they share at least one covered x, i.e. ``max(start_a, start_b)
  < min(end_a, end_b)``). Merely-touching neighbours (one interval's end
  equal to the next one's start) are currently left as separate intervals.

Public API:
  add(start, end), intervals(), raw(), contains(x)
"""


class IntervalSet:
    def __init__(self):
        # Canonical store: sorted by start, pairwise non-overlapping (touching
        # endpoints permitted for now), every interval non-empty.
        self._intervals = []

    def add(self, start, end):
        """Insert [start, end), coalescing it into the canonical form.

        Empty intervals (start >= end) are ignored. Intervals that merely
        touch the new interval (end == next start) are not merged.
        """
        if start >= end:
            return
        lo, hi = start, end
        merged = []
        placed = False
        for a, b in self._intervals:
            if a >= hi:
                # Interval starts at/after the growing span ends: touch or
                # beyond, so it stays separate -- drop the span in first.
                if not placed:
                    merged.append((lo, hi))
                    placed = True
                merged.append((a, b))
            elif b <= lo:
                # Interval ends at/before the span starts: touch or behind.
                merged.append((a, b))
            else:
                # Strictly overlaps the growing span: coalesce it in.
                lo = min(lo, a)
                hi = max(hi, b)
        if not placed:
            merged.append((lo, hi))
        self._intervals = merged

    def intervals(self):
        """Return the sorted, merged list of (start, end) tuples."""
        return list(self._intervals)

    def raw(self):
        """Backwards-compatible alias of intervals(): the merged, sorted form.

        (With a canonical store there is no longer an insertion-order history;
        this name is kept so callers of the seed API keep working.)
        """
        return list(self._intervals)

    def contains(self, x):
        """True iff any interval covers x (start <= x < end)."""
        for s, e in self._intervals:
            if s <= x < e:
                return True
        return False
